record.title: Reflection releases Beam 1.0 as a 501B-parameter open-weight model
record.summary: Reflection released Beam 1.0 weights on October 16 under Apache 2.0, with BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 variants. Its model card lists a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 501.3B total and 23.4B active parameters and a 1M-token context window. Reflection reports strong coding, reasoning and tool-use benchmark scores, but these remain vendor-run results without an independent reproduction. A linked safety report rates the model Limited across four systemic-risk categories while disclosing narrow, mixed evaluations and important sample and task limits.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Reflection's October 16 release post links publicly available Beam weights under Apache 2.0; the official model card lists BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 variants.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The model card describes Beam as a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 501.3B total parameters, 23.4B active parameters, 52 layers and a 1M-token context window.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Reflection reports scores of 81.6% on SWE-bench Verified and 80.1% on Terminal Bench 2.1, alongside results on reasoning and tool-use benchmarks. These are provider-reported results; no independent reproduction was performed.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Reflection's safety report assigns Beam a Limited rating across four systemic-risk categories and includes evaluations from named external providers. The report also describes a 20-participant human biological-uplift study as statistically non-significant and not wet-lab validated, and reports elevated performance on a narrow text-only pathogen-knowledge test; neither finding establishes real-world operational capability or its absence.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: No independent execution of the released weights, reproduction of vendor benchmark scores, or independent audit of the safety report was conducted in this review.

brief.importance_rationale: If the release delivers competitive agentic capability in a widely usable open-weight model, it could broaden access to frontier-scale inference and affect model-selection and deployment choices. The consequence is notable but not field-shifting: it is one provider's release, total parameter scale implies substantial deployment demands, and performance and economics remain first-party and unreproduced.
limitations: All reported benchmark scores and the overall safety assessment are from Reflection or named providers cited in its report; this review did not independently reproduce them.
A 1M-token context specification does not establish quality or cost across that full context length.
The 501.3B total parameter count may impose substantial memory and serving requirements; actual deployment hardware, throughput, latency and cost were not measured here.

The safety report's Limited ratings apply to specific evaluation regimes. Its human biological-uplift trial used 20 participants, was explicitly not statistically significant and lacked wet-lab validation; selected knowledge scores measure narrow test performance, not operational capability.
No evidence here establishes real-world adoption, customer outcomes, or the generalization of benchmark performance across tasks and harnesses.
brief.summary: Reflection released Beam 1.0 weights on October 16 under Apache 2.0, with BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 variants. Its model card lists a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 501.3B total and 23.4B active parameters and a 1M-token context window. Reflection reports strong coding, reasoning and tool-use benchmark scores, but these remain vendor-run results without an independent reproduction. A linked safety report rates the model Limited across four systemic-risk categories while disclosing narrow, mixed evaluations and important sample and task limits.

technical.claimed_result: Reflection reports strong performance across coding, reasoning and tool-use tests, including 81.6% on SWE-bench Verified and 80.1% on Terminal Bench 2.1. Its safety report rates Beam Limited across four systemic-risk categories; it also reports mixed task outcomes, including elevated performance on a narrow text-only pathogen-knowledge test and a statistically non-significant 20-person human-uplift comparison.
technical.compute_or_cost: Total parameter count is 501.3B, despite 23.4B active per token. This review did not establish minimum serving hardware, throughput, latency, energy, memory requirements or cost per task.
technical.demonstrated_result: The first-party announcement and model repository expose the released weights, Apache 2.0 license, numerical variants and model-card specifications. The existence and accessibility of the release are directly inspectable; benchmark performance and safety ratings are source-reported rather than independently demonstrated here.
technical.implementation_status: Weights are publicly listed under Apache 2.0, with linked hosted platforms and open-source integrations. The model card lists the released variants; it does not establish broad real-world use or low-cost local deployment.
technical.mechanism: A sparse mixture-of-experts language model with 501.3B total parameters and 23.4B active parameters per token, according to the official model card. Reflection's release introduces downloadable weights and an ecosystem of integrations for post-training, inference and agentic tooling.
technical.novelty: Reflection's first open-weight release combines a large sparse model, a 1M-token context claim and a broad partner/integration launch. Its benchmark positioning is vendor-reported and needs independent comparison.
technical.regime: Instruction-tuned text model in BF16, FP8 and NVFP4; model card lists 501.3B total parameters, 23.4B active parameters, 52 layers and a 1M-token context. Most benchmark and safety outcomes are Reflection-reported and tied to the named tasks, tools, prompts and model settings.
technical.reproducibility: Weights and model card are publicly available, but the research desk did not download/run the model or reproduce capability, safety or efficiency scores. The safety report links some named external evaluations, but the underlying evidence was not independently retrieved or audited.
technical.strongest_baseline: The model card compares Beam across BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 variants on listed public benchmarks; the safety report compares with a selected set of open-weight systems. No independent matched benchmark or deployment-cost comparison was conducted in this review.

brief.title: Reflection releases Beam 1.0 as a 501B-parameter open-weight model
brief.why_it_matters: Publicly downloadable weights and a permissive license extend access to a very large model from a new provider, while its sparse active-parameter count and reported agentic results make it relevant to open-model and inference choices. Actual serving costs, independent capability levels and safety performance remain unmeasured here, so the release does not yet establish that its reported quality is economical or generalizes beyond the tested settings.
